relevance_note: Case report of a Chinese boy with a TNFAIP3 frameshift ("Whole exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous mutation in the affected TNFAIP3 gene"), plus a literature table of 15 previously reported pediatric HA20 cases.
method_note: Read the whole paper by eye. I typed the values by hand into a Python script in my scratch directory, which builds the JSON. The script checks that every Table 3 row I re-typed matches a line of the paper exactly, and that every span occurs verbatim. The only change it makes to a typed span is to swap an ordinary space for the paper's non-breaking space where the paper has one. Labels: the first-hand case is labelled 'patient' (the paper's only first-hand patient is unnamed; Figure 1 calls him 'the first witness', i.e. the proband). His relatives are 'the father' and 'the mother'. Table 3 has patients as rows. Each label is the number in its 'Patients' cell; the parenthesised reference number in that cell goes into source_reference_in_review, together with the matching reference-list entry. The reference list is run together with the DOIs in the Markdown, so I matched numbers to entries by reading. Table 3 'Age (y)' is age at diagnosis per the table note. Decimal ages are kept as decimal years (P5.1Y, P4.6Y), not converted to months. Table 3 Y/N cells: Y = observed and N = excluded, for that column's feature only. For the checklist, N under 'Recurrent oral ulcers', 'Recurrent genital ulcers', 'Rash', 'Arthritis' or 'GI ulcers' leaves the broader checklist item 'not reported' (narrow-vs-broad rule). Only 'Recurrent fever' N excludes a checklist item. Checklist mappings I judged: 'Insulin-dependent diabetes' maps to type 1 diabetes; 'Autoimmune thyroid disorder' maps to autoimmune thyroiditis; 'small vessel CNS vasculitis' maps to both CNS involvement and vasculitis; 'growth delay' maps to growth failure. I did not map 'cytopenias' or 'hepatitis', because the paper does not call them autoimmune. I also did not map 'Hypothyroidism', or 'Pericardial effusion' to serositis. 'Pharyngalgia lymphadenopathy' is one cell with no comma; I split it into two features. publications.cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true refers only to the 15 Table 3 literature cases. The first-hand patient is not said to have been reported before (the paper says of his variant 'this mutation has not been reported before'). n_patients_reported = 1 counts the first-hand case only, since the paper never states a combined total. Not given rows: the grandparents ('This child's grandparents tested negative for the gene'), because their number and side of the family are not stated. Variants: the father carries the TNFAIP3 variant ('derived from the father'), but his zygosity and its origin are not stated. The mother was sequenced (Figure 1C), but her result is not stated explicitly, so she has no variant row. The alpha-thalassemia 'SEA deletion' in Table 2 is recorded as a non-TNFAIP3 variant for the patient; the paper prints no gene symbol for it. Lab abnormalities are recorded only when the text calls them abnormal or elevated. IgG 19.3, ESR 25 and hemoglobin 104 are outside the printed reference ranges but the text does not comment on them, so they are not recorded. Ages: the only age given for the first-hand patient is '3 years and 6 months old' at admission. His fever began '10 days ago'. Diagnosis by exome came later in the admission, and the last visit was about 11 months later. So onset, diagnosis and last-evaluation ages are all left 'not reported'. 'Oral mucosa was smooth' at admission, and oral ulcers appeared later. I did not treat this as a contradiction and emitted no excluded row. The meaning of 'pendulous ulcers' is unclear, so I recorded it verbatim and did not map it to genital ulcers. CONTRADICTIONS AND INCONSISTENCIES IN THE PAPER: (1) The literature summary says 'six (40%) were male and nine (60%) were female', but Table 3 lists 9 M and 6 F; each person's sex is taken from Table 3. (2) The Discussion says there were 'no special abnormalities in rheumatologic immune indicators', yet also that the patient 'presented with abnormalities in the indicators, including antinuclear antibodies ... anti-neutrophilic cytoplasmic antibodies' (Table 1: ANA 33.3, P-ANCA weakly positive). I treated the first statement as non-specific and recorded autoantibodies as observed. (3) The text says 'IL-6, IL-4, and IL-10 all showed elevations', but Table 1 has no IL-10 value. (4) The text says 'high IgE and IgA on admission', but the Table 1 IgA of 1.47 g/L lies inside the printed range of 1.45–3.45. (5) Table 3 patient 4, age 4, cites ref (4), whose title is 'A case of adult-onset still's disease ...', although the review says it excluded adult-onset cases. (6) Grandparents testing negative is said to suggest 'the mutation came from the father'. I left the father's inheritance 'not reported'. (7) The cardiopulmonary examination at admission showed 'no significant abnormality', while the echocardiogram showed a patent foramen ovale and mild valve insufficiency. These are different methods, so I recorded both.
